title: Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography for Functional Imaging in Vascular Research
protocol: Turn on the optoacoustic imaging equipment.
Introduce participant information while the equipment is warming up.
Click Patient ID in the main welcome window of the software.
Enter data including name, study denomination, personal data, and any relevant observations.
Press Select to finish entering the application data.
Preset selection: Make sure the Laser is Ready message appears on the equipment screen.
Wait for the laser status bar to change from Laser Standby to Laser is Ready.
Ensure every participant in the room applies laser safety goggles.
Press the laser (power) switch foot pedal and wait for the laser power self-check.
Release the check-up report window by pressing the OK button.
Positioning and Image Acquisition: Acclimatize the participant to the laboratory environment (21 °C ± 1 °C; 40%-60% relative humidity).
Choose a comfortable position to minimize unnecessary movement.
Ensure that the area to be scanned is previously cleaned.
Apply a thin layer of ultrasound gel to the 3D cup.
Position and stabilize a lockable arm for the area of interest.
Securely lock the 3D cup positioning arm.
Push the manufacturer's default preset Hb, HbO2, and Melanin that simultaneously measures chromophores for Hb, HbO2, and melanin.
Select the anatomical area for baseline image acquisition.
Press the laser footswitch pedal to start image acquisition.
Press the View button on the touchscreen to display the live image.
Capture a snapshot of the stable image by pressing the Snapshot button when image stability is maximized.
Continue pressing the laser footswitch pedal for continuous video acquisition.
Record the live image by pressing the Record button.
Press the Stop button on the optoacoustic imaging platform.
Adjust the pressure cuff to the patient's arm above the elbow.
Inflate the cuff with supra systolic pressure (~200 mmHg).
Acquire the imaged vasculature under pressure according to steps 2.3.1 to 2.3.3.1.
Open the pressure valve while acquiring a video as in step 2.3.3.2.
Follow the live image on the screen during acquisition.
Copy recorded scans to a selected/dedicated folder for backup and further analysis.
Use manufacturer's dedicated analytical software for scan analysis on a separate computer workstation.
Order scans by acquisition time within the study folder with a running code.
Open the analysis program on the workstation computer.
Choose program Menu > Open Study to import files and access backup scans.
Scroll to the bottom of the folder containing recorded scans.
Identify files with a .NOD extension for opening studies.
Ensure that the program workflow tabs are visible (colored black) on the top menu bar: Menu; Scan Overview; Reconstruction; Fluence Correction; Spectral Unmixing; Visualization & Analysis.
Activate necessary workflow tabs, which turn blue upon activation.
Reconstruct the image via the Reconstruction tab of the software.
Select the scans to reconstruct from the left side of the main program menu.
Leave the default six optoacoustic emission wavelengths (700, 730, 760, 800, 850, and 900 nm).
Perform the scan reconstruction using the icon on the right side.
Select the Scan preset and Field of View (resolution) as prompted by the program workflow.
Adjust the speed of sound to adjust scan focus.
Push the button Reconstruct Scans at the top of the screen to advance to scan reconstruction.
After finishing the reconstruction, advance to Fluence Correction for image post-processing analysis.
Activate Fluence Correction in the dashboard menu.
Load reconstructed images for fluence correction.
Select files with a flag next to each scan number.
Display selected reconstructions on the right side of the screen.
Push the Save Fluence Correction button to proceed.
Perform spectral unmixing of acquired preset (Hb, HbO2, and melanin).
Select the Spectral Unmixing tab.
Open the list of Selected Reconstructions for spectral unmixing.
Display scans with history of previous image processing steps on the right side.
Load previously saved fluence correction files.
Activate spectral unmixing by pushing the icon.
Observe the wavelengths to be unmixed.
Choose six optoacoustic emission wavelengths for spectral unmixing: 700 nm, 730 nm, 760 nm, 800 nm, 850 nm, and 900 nm.
Edit desired spectra using the XYZ icon if necessary.
Confirm adjusted parameters.
Click Start Spectral Unmixing to begin processing.
Display a processing menu bar showing operation progress.
Access the Visualization and Analysis tab.
Click an activated scan to display subject information and comments.
Create a multiple scan analysis by pushing the + button.
Introduce a multiple scan view and press Save.
Select each desired scan to add to the saved Analysis View.
Add additional scans at the top left corner icon for automatic display in the Analysis View.
Set proper color lookup tables to prepare the image for analysis.
Click More Image Control Options on the top menu bar and activate the Max Intensity Projection icon.
Attribute colors to layers by pressing the icon available in the bottom right corner of the image display, adjacent to the 2D+ image display.
Select More to edit the colors of all channels simultaneously.
Adjust each layer's color intensity with the tools available at the bottom left of the screen.
Identify the ROI to be analyzed.
Surround the ROI with shapes available in the menu bar in the XY image while tracing the same ROI within the orthogonal views available in the XZ and YZ axis.
Follow the ROI shape in the remaining XZ and YZ axis using the Add Interpolate and Remove sub-regions function.
Import Region of Interest to Quantification.
Observe multi spectra component for selected ROI on screen.
Export ROI data by pressing Excel icon at bottom of graphical view.
Press TIFF file export option from menu to export images with embedded data and built-in ROI outline.
